title: pinned-version-eval-fanout-and-priority-throttler
creator: Sofia Chen
body:
Goal: Build a centralized eval fanout service that launches targeted eval jobs when a catalog model or tenant-pinned model version changes, and which applies a priority-based throttling policy to stay within budget and infra limits.

Background: We currently run ad-hoc and several different automated eval flows for model promotions and pin changes. There are gaps: noisy bursts when many tenants pin simultaneously, inability to prioritize high-risk tenants or high-importance catalogs, and lack of a consistent backpressure mechanism to avoid blowing eval budgets or saturating dedicated infra. This ticket scopes a product design and acceptance criteria for an orchestration layer that can: 1) decide which evals to run, 2) schedule them with tenant/catalog priorities and budget caps, 3) surface results and signals to the Console and rollout logic (canary/fallback paths).

High-level approach: Implement a "fanout-and-throttle" service that listens to pin/catalog-change events, enriches events with tenant priority and cost constraints, and enqueues eval runners. The service will consult sampling policies (probe sets, smoke vs. full fidelity), a tenant SLA/priority table, and a system rate limiter. It will emit a deterministic eval plan and provide a cancel/backoff API for downstream workers. The product scope for this ticket focuses on the evaluation selection rules, priority policy, and acceptance criteria; engineering tickets will follow for the runtime implementation and infra work.
acceptance_criteria: When a catalog or tenant pin change occurs the fanout service produces an eval plan within 30s that lists eval jobs and priorities for the affected tenants.
Policy rules allow marking tenants as high/medium/low priority; high-priority tenants are guaranteed quicker scheduling and higher sample budgets with a configurable cap.
System-level rate limiter prevents more than the configured eval token budget per hour (global and per-region) and gracefully backpressures lower-priority jobs.
Eval plans are persisted and visible in Console under the pin-change event detail with links to the running eval jobs and their status.
The service emits structured events to the audit log and provides a rollout signal (pass/fail/needs-investigation) that is consumed by the pin promotion workflow.
Automated smoke evals for tenant-pinned changes run for at least 90% of pins by default unless tenant opts out; heavy/full evals are sampled or require manual approval per policy.
Integration tests exist that simulate burst pin changes for 500 tenants and demonstrate backpressure prevents exceeding the defined budget and that priorities influence scheduling order.
tasks: Define priority and budget model (policy draft) and map to Console UI fields
Design event enrichment: tenant metadata, SLA, and sample profile lookups
Proto eval plan schema and persistence contract with Console and audit logs
Specify rate limiting and token-bucket rules (global, regional, per-tenant backoff)
Create API contract for eval runner workers: accept plan, report progress, cancel/backoff
Write integration tests and stress tests for burst scenarios
Document default sampling profiles (smoke vs full) and opt-out/opt-in controls for tenants
comments: 2025-02-14 - Sofia Chen: Drafted scope after sync with SRE and Console PM. Key decision: default to smoke evals for tenant pins and reserve full evals for catalog/promotions.
2025-02-20 - Miguel Alvarez: Requested clear SLA mapping and a UI surface for tenants to set opt-out flags. Need to confirm default sample rates with Research.
2025-02-25 - Asha Patel: Engineering prefers to implement priority/throttle as a separate microservice to keep eval runners stateless. Will raise ENG tasks after PM sign-off.
2025-03-01 - Lina Morales: Console will add an 'Eval activity' tab on the pin event detail; design will supply mocks by 2025-03-10.
2025-03-03 - Miguel Alvarez: Updated acceptance criteria to include visible persisted plans and forced integration tests for burst scenarios. Marking ready for design review.
